pages.chapter: The Fox That Was Not a Fox
pages.text: Julia sat on the back step with her snack. Toby sat on the grass next to her. It was a hot, still day. Toby was thinking.
pages.picture: a hot, quiet afternoon in Julia's backyard: Julia on the back step of the house with a bowl of crackers; Toby lying on the lawn beside her, eyes half closed, deep in thought

pages.text: Then the grass at the gate shook. A fox slid under the gate! It ran right up to Julia, took her snack, and dashed off.
pages.picture: a red fox slipping under the wooden garden gate and snatching a cracker from Julia's bowl; Julia surprised, Toby lifting his head

pages.text: "Stop!" said Julia. The fox froze. It looked back at Julia, right at her, as if it had met her. Julia felt a chill.
pages.picture: the fox frozen on the lawn with the snack in its mouth, looking back over its shoulder straight at Julia; a faint pink, green and blue shimmer in its red fur, easy to miss; Julia uneasy

pages.text: Then a boy jumped down from the next yard. It was Max. "I will get it!" he yelled. He ran after the fox. Bang! He ran smack into Toby.
pages.picture: Max, a bold eight-year-old boy, has leapt down from the neighbour's fence and is running flat out after the fox, about to crash into Toby's side

pages.text: Max sat on the grass. He looked up at Toby. Julia held still. "A dragon!" said Max. "Can I ride him? Can I get up on his back?"
pages.picture: Max sitting on the lawn looking up at Toby, thrilled, reaching out a hand; Toby shy, ducking his nose; Julia frozen, worried

pages.text: Julia held his hand. "Can you keep this hush-hush?" "Yes! But the fox!" said Max. The fox was at the end of the backyard. Then it was in the woods.
pages.picture: Julia holding Max's hand, finger to her lips, serious; Max pointing past her at the far end of the backyard where the fox slips through the back gate into the woods

pages.text: They ran after it. Max shot up a tree to look. Toby crashed past the ferns. Julia bent down and looked for tracks in the mud.
pages.picture: in the woods: Max climbing high up a tree to look out; Toby pushing through the ferns; Julia crouching by small paw prints in the mud

pages.text: "There!" said Julia. "The pond!" At the pond, the tracks went into the mud. Then they just ended. No fox. Not in the reeds. Not in the trees.
pages.picture: by the woodland pond: a line of fox paw prints in the mud that simply ends; Julia, Max and Toby looking around, puzzled; no fox anywhere

pages.text: "Is it in the pond?" said Max. Julia bent down. The tracks did not go on. They did not go back. "A fox can not just stop," she said.
pages.picture: Julia crouched by the last paw print in the mud, frowning, thinking hard; Max scratching his head; Toby peering into the reeds

pages.text: That night, they sat down to eat. Julia stood up with her Dragon Book. "Look," she said. In it was a fox, its tracks, and a big "?"
pages.picture: evening, the family kitchen table: Mom and Dad at dinner, Max at the table too; Julia standing, holding up her Dragon Book open to her crayon drawing of a fox, a line of paw prints that ends, and a big question mark; Toby's head peeking in at the open back door

pages.text: Max jumped up on his chair. "It was this big! It bit me! I got up on Toby!" "It did not bite you," said Julia. "Max, sit," said Mom.
pages.picture: Max standing on his chair at the table, arms spread wide, telling the story far too loudly; Julia with her hand on her forehead; Mom pointing at his chair; Dad trying not to laugh

pages.text: Then Mom said, "A kid starts in your class in the morning, Julia. He just got here." Julia looked down at her Dragon Book. At the big "?"
pages.picture: close on Julia at the table looking down at the question mark in her Dragon Book, thoughtful; Mom soft behind her; dusk outside the window
